Ldensity.title: Dynamics of quadratic polynomials, I–II
Ldensity.quote: Any real quadratic polynomial P_c without attracting cycles is rigid on the real line. Thus hyperbolic quadratics are dense on the real line.
Ldensity.hypotheses: Real quadratic polynomial P_c(z)=z²+c, c real, without attracting cycles; real rigidity is defined immediately above as Com(c)∩R={c}.
Ldensity.statement: Real rigidity under these hypotheses and density of real hyperbolic quadratics. Not complex combinatorial rigidity.
Ldensity.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

L.title: Dynamics of quadratic polynomials, I–II
L.locator: Rigidity Theorem p. 187; §2.5 pp. 198–199 (PDF pp. 14–15); Theorem IV′ (prior locator only)
L.hypotheses: At most one member of a fixed combinatorial class can simultaneously satisfy the secondary-limbs condition (all straightened renormalizations in finitely many truncated secondary limbs) and a priori bounds (uniform positive fundamental modulus).
L.statement: Uniqueness among members satisfying BOTH assumptions; to conclude a singleton entire class requires the assumptions for every member. §2.5 describes the maximal-copy nest and states the global MLC/rigidity equivalence for infinitely renormalizable parameters; not a blanket pointwise topological-LC-to-fiber theorem.
L.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

Lreal.title: Dynamics of quadratic polynomials, I–II
Lreal.hypotheses: Infinitely renormalizable real quadratic polynomial; essential periods of all renormalizations exceed a fixed universal threshold.
Lreal.statement: MLC at the real parameter. Proof compares all complex parameters with the same real combinatorics; not arbitrary real parameters with unbounded relative periods.
Lreal.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

LY.title: Dynamics of quadratic polynomials: complex bounds for real maps

LY.hypotheses: Real quadratic parameter in the connected real range for the Julia-set assertion; complex bounds theorem uses sufficiently deep real renormalizations with the doubling/cusp qualification.
LY.statement: Complex bounds and Julia-set local connectivity, not all-real parameter-space MLC.
LY.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

DL26.title: MLC at Feigenbaum points
DL26.locator: Theorems A and B p. 3; relative periods p. 11
DL26.quote: The Mandelbrot set is locally connected at any Feigenbaum parameter.
DL26.hypotheses: Feigenbaum = infinitely renormalizable quadratic-like map with bounded relative renormalization periods, not merely bounded CF digits or bounded primitive gaps.
DL26.statement: A priori beau bounds and MLC for bounded relative periods, with singleton nested-copy intersection noted on p. 3.
DL26.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

Lev1.title: Rigidity and non-local connectivity of Julia sets of some quadratic polynomials
Lev1.hypotheses: Infinitely renormalizable quadratic; increasing renormalization periods n_m with simple renormalizations and reduced rotation p_m/q_m in (−1/2,1/2]; limsup log|p_m|/n_m>0, or the satellite variant with limsup log q_m/n_m>0.
Lev1.statement: MLC at the parameter under the indicated growth condition.
Lev1.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

Lev2.title: Rigidity and non-local connectivity of Julia sets of some quadratic polynomials
Lev2.hypotheses: Successive satellite bifurcations of a hyperbolic component at reduced nonzero rotations t_m=p_m/q_m; q_m→∞ and limsup |t_m|^(1/q_(m−1))<1.
Lev2.statement: Convergence of the cascade to c*, MLC at c* and non-local-connectivity of its Julia set.
Lev2.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

Levadd.title: Addendum to: Rigidity and non-local connectivity of Julia sets of some quadratic polynomials

Levadd.statement: MLC at the limiting parameter; no assertion on the complement.

EE.title: A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratics: IV. Elephant eyes
EE.locator: §4.0.1 E1–E3 p. 9; §8 pp. 18–19, unnumbered MLC assertion
EE.quote: MLC at the corresponding parameter values follows from the machinery developed in [L1]
EE.hypotheses: Even quadratic-like map with connected Julia set and both fixed points repelling; E1 dividing fixed point rotation 1/q, q>1, and the prescribed sector return/degree pattern (central branch degree 2, intervening branches univalent); E2 only central little filled Julia set K0 lies in central domain; E3 p=q+b, b uniformly bounded, simplifying assumption b<q. Infinitely renormalizable elephant-eye family at every level, not just the numerical identity.
EE.statement: The §8 MLC assertion for the corresponding parameters; outline invokes [L1], cylinder-copy input [C,DLP], and further work with Kapiamba (p. 19 n. 5). No independent proof or singleton parameter fiber established here.
EE.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

KKL.authors: Jeremy Kahn; Alex Kapiamba; Mikhail Lyubich
KKL.title: MLC for parabolically bounded primitive renormalization
KKL.venue: IMS preprint 26-02; arXiv:2606.27272; no journal record found
KKL.locator: Theorem C p. 4; definition of rigidity and Theorems A/B p. 3; §3.1 p. 19; §7 p. 56; bibliography p. 71
KKL.quote: Any parabolically bounded family of prime primitive types is rigid.
KKL.hypotheses: All levels prime primitive; types lie in a finite union of fixed types and parabolic tails with balanced limb insertion (both k_q and q−k_q tend to infinity). Theorem B requires beau bounds AND bounded puzzle Teichmüller diameter, and DKLP is cited for the latter on tails.
KKL.statement: Theorem C gives rigidity in the authors’ p. 3 meaning of MLC. The authors distinguish combinatorial rigidity in §7; no separate verified singleton parameter-fiber assertion for the downgraded finite-prefix application. Remark p. 4 does not claim general mixed extension.
KKL.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

CS2015.title: Satellite renormalization of quadratic polynomials
CS2015.version: v1 (25 Sep 2015), listed arXiv version; later author revision below
CS2015.locator: Theorem D p. 6; QG_N equation (44) p. 62
CS2015.quote: it is combinatorially rigid, and the Mandelbrot set is locally connected at c.
CS2015.hypotheses: Nonzero reduced satellite rotations p_i/q_i represented in (−1/2,1/2], signed continued-fraction digits b_i,j; for some universal N, b_1,1≥N, b_i,j+1≥b_i,j², and b_i+1,1≥q_i² for every level; all-satellite PL-renormalization. Full signed-CF QG_N, not simply unbounded digits.
CS2015.statement: There exist N,C>0 and 0<λ<1 such that for each sequence in QG_N the whole nested copies have diameter at most Cλ^n; unique intersection parameter, combinatorial rigidity and MLC.

TUN.title: On fibers and renormalization of Julia sets and Multibrot sets
TUN.quote: The fiber of any point in the Multibrot set is trivial if and only if
TUN.hypotheses: Canonical tuning map from Multibrot set to a little copy; trivial parameter fiber of a point (or equivalently its tuned image).
TUN.statement: Triviality of parameter fibers is preserved in both directions by tuning. This transfers CS D singleton intersections through a finite prefix; a bare pointwise LC assertion does not supply the hypothesis.
TUN.hash_provenance: Inherited byte digest from #134 sources.json; not re-downloaded or compared with the opened rendering.

TUNscope.title: On fibers and local connectivity of Mandelbrot and Multibrot sets
TUNscope.locator: Abstract; §7 Proposition 7.4 (HTML; PDF page not checked)
TUNscope.quote: Locally, triviality of fibers is strictly stronger than local connectivity.
TUNscope.hypotheses: Pointwise local connectivity versus trivial fibers; non-hyperbolic combinatorial classes in the stated rational-lamination definition.
TUNscope.statement: Trivial fibers imply LC; outside hyperbolic combinatorial classes the classes are fibers. No inference from bare pointwise LC to singleton parameter fiber.
